plan.title: Paired 3-condition DE: treatment A/B vs control + treatment comparison
plan.analytical_narrative: Four subjects each contribute a control, treated_a, and treated_b blood sample (raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, single batch). Because subject is a repeated-measures blocking factor with three within-subject conditions, the grounded procedure (Inflexa rule R-0069/R-0011) is a DESeq2 fit with design ~subject+condition: a likelihood-ratio test (full ~subject+condition vs reduced ~subject) answers 'does this gene respond to either treatment within a subject', and named pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b) with ashr-shrunken log2FC answer 'do the two treatments differ from each other and from control'. QC precedes modeling (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to confirm subjects pair correctly and no sample is a clustering outlier before trusting the paired design. Each contrast is filtered/tested independently (BH within contrast, R-0061) since three groups mean three separate questions. Downstream, GO/Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways over-representation on each contrast's significant gene list is the enrichment method the knowledge service names as permitted for a discrete gene-list input here (fgsea preranked GSEA was flagged as not permitted for this profile by the knowledge check; ORA with the tested-gene universe is used instead, gated on each contrast having at least the ~50 significant genes ORA needs for power). A decoupleR ulm transcription-factor activity pass on the CollecTRI human regulons, run on the Wald statistic of each contrast, adds a regulator-level view of what is driving the response. All reference collections and packages named below were confirmed present in this environment before drafting.
